title: Oven-Roasted Silky Filipino Tofu Kare-Kare
description: A creative twist on the classic Filipino dish, using silky tofu and a braising liquid for a rich and comforting flavor. Perfect for a Buddhist temple-friendly meal, served in a traditional terracotta dish.
instructions: In a large terracotta dish, combine the chopped onion, grated ginger, minced garlic, and chopped peanuts.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a skillet over medium heat and sauté the onion mixture until fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Add the chopped bok choy to the skillet and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.
In a blender or food processor, combine the peanut sauce, coconut milk, curry powder, black pepper, and turmeric. Blend until smooth.
Pour the peanut sauce mixture over the bok choy mixture in the terracotta dish.
Cut the silky tofu into 1-inch cubes and arrange on top of the peanut sauce mixture.
Pour in the chicken broth and cover the terracotta dish with aluminum foil.
Transfer the terracotta dish to the preheated oven and braise for 25 minutes.
Remove the foil and continue to roast for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the tofu is golden brown and the sauce has thickened.
Remove from the oven and let it rest for a few minutes before serving.
Garnish with chopped peanuts and serve over steamed rice or noodles.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
